title: UGC creators: why phone footage outsells your polished ad
description: User-generated content converts better than studio ads. How to find creators, what to pay them, and how to turn one video into ten test variants.
excerpt: Brands drop five figures on a commercial nobody watches to the end. Meanwhile a video shot on a phone in someone's kitchen outsells it. Here's why.
content:
If you've got an ad budget and want the most out of it, stop paying for a polished spot and start paying real people to talk about your product into a phone. User-generated content beats studio production in paid social, and it isn't close.

## Why it works

People clock an ad within half a second and keep scrolling. UGC looks like a friend's post, so it gets a chance to land. Brands that switch from produced video to UGC routinely see cost per click drop by a third — not because the video is better, but because it doesn't read as advertising.

## How to find creators

Don't filter by follower count. Filter by whether they can talk to a camera. Search hashtags in your category, pick 20 people with 1k–10k followers who sound natural on video, and DM them directly. A single UGC video runs roughly $80–200 — and you own it, so you can run it as an ad.

## Turn one video into ten

Brief each creator on three different hooks for the same script. You get three openings on one core message, which means three ads to test for the price of one shoot. Then hand the winning hook to more creators and repeat.

When a UGC video starts working organically, giving it early momentum helps — some creators and brands use [KupSledujici](https://kupsledujici.cz) to push strong content while the algorithm is still deciding its reach. And when you find a winner worth running abroad, [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) dubs it into 50+ languages, so one shoot covers ten markets.

Commission three UGC videos this week. You'll learn what your audience actually wants to hear faster than any analytics dashboard will tell you.
